home.title: How quantum matter changes fields—and how gravity enters.
home.intro: Explore a tested model in which an electric field creates a quantum current, and that current changes the field. Follow the evidence toward a future calculation in evolving spacetime.
home.status: Restricted model tested · full Einstein–QED problem open
home.guideTitle: Use this workspace in three steps

steps.title: Understand the feedback
steps.text: Read the physical picture, then expand the equations when you are ready.

steps.title: Inspect a result and its tests
steps.text: Compare a recorded trajectory with its numerical checks and the exact model assumptions.

steps.title: Choose a test that could prove an idea wrong
steps.text: Open an experiment, inspect its null comparison and rejection gate, and record what is still needed.

features.title: Computed field history
features.plain: The source first drives the electric field. After the source stops, the quantum current continues to change the field and eventually reverses its direction in this model.
features.how: Inspect the field curve, then open its source, data and model details. Use the data table for exact saved values.
features.technical: Homogeneous Maxwell–Dirac mean field with static magnetic field. x=eE/m², s=mt. The final recorded run uses b=10, canonical window ±40, 4096 momentum nodes and Landau levels 0–8.
features.meaning: A computed trajectory within a tested finite model. It is not a measured field, a continuum bound or a solved spacetime.
features.scope: Flat metric; constant homogeneous magnetic field; expectation-value electromagnetic backreaction

features.title: Does the result survive refinement?
features.plain: A curve can conserve energy accurately while its momentum grid is still too coarse. Compare the separate tests before deciding which digits to trust.
features.how: Compare the final fixed-window grids and read the separate Landau-level check. Open failed historical gates to see what changed.
features.technical: The 2048→4096 fixed-window sampled field history differs by 3.26e−9. A separate levels 0–8→0–12 comparison shifts the endpoint by 5.06e−8. These are distinct component changes.
features.meaning: Measured refinement differences, not a statistical confidence interval or a rigorous bound on all numerical and physical errors.

features.title: Coherence and phase mismatch
features.plain: Two coupled waves can exchange amplitude. If their phases drift apart, conversion is limited in this constant, lossless model.
features.how: Change dimensionless coupling and phase mismatch. Predict the direction of the change before computing, then compare with exact resonance.
features.technical: Let u=μL and v=δL. Then P=u² sinc²(√(u²+v²/4)), where sinc z=sin(z)/z and sinc 0=1. μ is the mixing amplitude and δ the propagation mismatch.
features.meaning: An exact analytic two-mode benchmark under a constant lossless matrix. It does not calculate a magnetar's full QED dispersion or gravitational signal.

features.title: Can the fields support the target curvature?
features.plain: Field strength and spacetime curvature are different scales. This calculator estimates the electromagnetic source budget and shows when another gravitating source is required.
features.how: Enter the electric and magnetic strengths in critical-field units. Read the source scale and the assumptions used to compute it.
features.technical: Use the reviewer-approved relation between κρ/m_e² and the electromagnetic energy density, with all constants and unit conventions visible.
features.meaning: A dimensional source-budget check. It does not solve Einstein's constraints or construct a supporting object.
features.implementationGate: Physics reviewer supplies and tests formula/constants before release

features.title: Four problems, shared dependencies
features.plain: Follow the four original questions and see what evidence each one still needs. A result in one geometry cannot automatically settle a problem in another.
features.how: Choose a research front. Inspect its assumptions, central equations, validated pieces and next discriminating test.
features.technical: Tracks charged de Sitter discharge, curved-space pair creation, Cauchy-horizon evolution and photon–graviton conversion, with state, renormalization and boundary-condition dependencies.
features.meaning: A dependency map and claim audit; completion indicators describe documented checks, not a percentage of physics solved.

features.title: Read a claim at its source
features.plain: Find the paper or document behind an equation, criticism or experiment. See what was actually inspected and which version was used.
features.how: Search by topic or author and filter by research front or reading depth. Open a source record for claim links, limitations and a direct primary link.
features.technical: Separate publication metadata, inspected sections, reproduced results and source access gaps. Preserve source dates and revision identifiers.
features.meaning: A targeted research ledger. Patent or government origin alone does not validate a physical claim.

features.title: Plan a test that could reject the hypothesis
features.plain: A useful experiment specifies what would change our mind before results are available.
features.how: Choose an experiment and inspect its comparison model, observable, rejection rule and prerequisites. Save your notes or export the plan where available.
features.technical: Prioritize common current/stress subtraction and quantum-response validity before coupling the metric. Record parameter ranges, tolerances and regulator checks separately.
features.meaning: A proposed research plan becomes executed only when code, data and reviewer evidence exist; reviewing a card does not validate the hypothesis.

features.title: How the advisor evaluates a result
features.plain: The advisor turns a broad question into bounded tasks, asks for independent objections, and accepts only the claims supported by the evidence.
features.how: Read the role pipeline and acceptance gates, then download the protocol for the next research cycle.
features.technical: Separate proposer, domain reviewer, numerical implementer and independent verifier; require source provenance, explicit scope and counterexample tests at handoffs.
features.meaning: A documented workflow and dated review record. This page does not imply a continuously running or autonomous agent service.
